subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: What verified-human provenance contract and sensitive-target enforcement surface should OpenClaw support for exec, gateway mutations, and outbound messaging?
rationale: The request defines a new security boundary plus config, plugin/API, and upgrade semantics; source inspection can prove the gap but cannot safely choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Core Gateway Policy
options.body: Define core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and stricter approval or denial fallback at the gateway/tool boundary.

options.title: Plugin Context First
options.body: Land safe hook facts such as action classification, input provenance, and source-aware context before letting a security plugin implement the policy.

options.title: Fold Into Taint Umbrella
options.body: Defer this request into the broader persistent-taint and content-derived execution guardrail design so maintainers choose one unified model.

recommendation.title: Core Gateway Policy
recommendation.body: Define core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit config/schema, provenance propagation, and stricter approval or denial fallback at the gateway/tool boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main routing signal is around hook contracts, trusted tool policy, and exec approval surfaces.
